extracted.intended_audience: students, educators, librarians, and general readers looking for Michael L. Printz Award-winning young adult books
extracted.subtask_description: A college library research guide that (1) defines the Michael L. Printz Award and its purpose and (2) lists Printz Award winners by year with bibliographic/location information for library users. Useful for locating and identifying YA titles recognized for literary excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: "The Michael L. Printz Award" criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Michael L. Printz Award is an award for a book that exemplifies literary excellence in young adult literature."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named for a Topeka, Kansas school librarian and administered by YALSA (link provided). This single-sentence definition is the page's explicit evaluative standard: eligible works are those in young adult literature demonstrating "literary excellence." No further scoring dimensions are provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement timing (procedural)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural note about the award cycle and when new winners become public; useful for understanding eligibility windows and for updating lists/catalogs annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic/listing format for winners in the guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Each listed winner entry includes the title, author, call number, and the year and designation (e.g., "2020 winner").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page demonstrates how the guide presents award-winning books to library users: include title, "by" author line, call number (physical or ebook), and the award year/status. Use this format when creating or updating library guides, catalogs, or reading lists to aid locateability and clarity.
